questions.q: In the capstone QLoRA setup, what is the role of BitsAndBytesConfig with load_in_4bit=True?
options: It quantizes the dataset's text labels to reduce storage size
It loads the base model in 4-bit precision, making a model like an 8B-parameter checkpoint trainable on a single GPU
It increases the model's context length automatically
It replaces the need for a LoraConfig entirely
questions.explain: 4-bit quantization of the frozen base model, as covered in the QLoRA lesson, reduces memory footprint enough to make fine-tuning a model of this size feasible on realistic single-GPU hardware.

questions.q: Why does the capstone fine-tune use a conservative, capped num_train_epochs value?
options: Because SFTTrainer does not support more than 3 epochs under any configuration
To apply the forgetting-aware ceiling from the catastrophic forgetting lesson, since a small, narrow dataset trained for too many epochs raises the risk of general-capability regression
Because more epochs always increase GPU memory usage beyond available limits
Because epoch count has no effect on fine-tuning outcomes
questions.explain: This directly applies the Chapter 4 lesson on catastrophic forgetting: more epochs over a small, narrow dataset increases forgetting risk, so capping epochs is a deliberate anti-forgetting choice, not an arbitrary default.

questions.q: What should be monitored during the fine-tune run, beyond the final training loss value?
options: Only the GPU's fan speed and temperature
Held-out loss, computed periodically against the split set aside before training, to catch the signature of overfitting -- training loss still falling while held-out loss flattens or rises
The number of parameters in the tokenizer's vocabulary
Nothing else needs to be monitored once training starts
questions.explain: Watching held-out loss during training, not just training loss, reveals overfitting: if training loss keeps falling while held-out loss flattens or rises, that's a signal to stop early rather than continue to a fixed epoch count.

questions.q: Why is what gets saved after this fine-tuning run a few hundred megabytes rather than a full copy of the base model?
options: Because the training run failed to save the full model due to an error
Because this is a LoRA adapter, not a full fine-tune -- only the small set of trainable adapter weights is saved, while the base model stays frozen and unmodified throughout
Because the base model was deleted after training completed
Because SFTTrainer always compresses saved checkpoints to a fixed small size
questions.explain: Since the base model's weights are frozen throughout LoRA fine-tuning, only the small set of adapter weights needs to be saved -- a direct consequence of PEFT's structural approach described in the SFT chapter.

questions.q: What specific prior lessons does the capstone fine-tune configuration directly combine?
options: Tokenization strategies and pretraining data pipelines only
QLoRA quantization, LoRA adapter configuration, and the forgetting-aware learning rate/epoch defaults, assembled together into one SFTTrainer run
Parallelism strategies and checkpointing at scale only
Benchmark contamination and human evaluation design only
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly wires together QLoRA's 4-bit quantization, LoRA's adapter configuration, and the conservative learning-rate/epoch defaults from the catastrophic forgetting lesson into a single runnable SFTTrainer configuration.
